headline: Approved 111 Winooski Falls Way sign master plan, authorized Downtown Winooski FY27 agreement, and made two commission appointments.
summary: Members approved the consent agenda, a sign plan and Act 250 application for 111 Winooski Falls Way, a Downtown Winooski agreement for FY27, and position descriptions for the fire department and Thrive program. Discussion covered impact fees and department updates on strategic vision goals, and no action was taken on them.
decisions: Approved consent agenda items, including meeting minutes and payroll and payables warrants, 4-0.
Approved appointments of James Paradissis and Jarron Khan, with Khan as a full-time appointment, 4-0.
Approved the 111 Winooski Falls Way sign master plan and approved submitting the Act 250 permit application, 4-0.
Authorized the City Manager to sign the FY27 memorandum of understanding with Downtown Winooski, with a change to item 1A, 4-0.
Approved the Assistant Fire Marshal and Career Lieutenant position descriptions, unanimously 4-0.
Approved the Thrive Program Assistant Director (part time) position description, 4-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Motion to approve Consent Agenda made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf. Motion passed 4-0.

A motion to approve James Paradissis and Jarron Khan, with Jarron being a full-time appointment as opposed to an alternate made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion passed 4-0.

Motion to approve the 111 Winooski Falls Way Sign Master Plan as presented and approve the application to submit the Act 250 Permit Application made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and seconded by Councilor Turkos. Motion passed 4-0.

A motion to authorize the City Manager to sign the FY27 MOU with Downtown Winooski as presented with the change of item 1A after annually to say may include a list of events subject to a schedule to be submitted by our March 31st meeting made by Councilor Goodrich and seconded by Councilor Turkos. Motion passed 4-0
Motion to approve the Assistant Fire Marshal and Career Lieutenant position descriptions as presented made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion passed unanimously 4-0.
Motion to approve the Thrive Program Assistant Director position description as presented made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf. Motion carried 4-0.

V. Council Reports 
Mayor Thomas Renner: The Planning Commission did not meet at the last meeting as it was canceled. 
They will be meeting on August 13th. A reminder that there is an election coming up on August 11th. You  
can vote at the Senior Center 7 AM to 7 PM sharp. Those doors will close at 7. There are lots of 
candidates to research and look for. I believe they all have social media where you can find out more 
information about them. There’s information now on the Secretary of State’s website. I encourage 
every member of our community who is able to vote to vote on that day. This is quite literally when 
you pick the people who will represent you in Montpelier and there are lots of repercussions to that. It’s 
very important to show up, circle those little ovals, and just figure out who the best candidate is for 
you. Again, August 11th, at the Senior Center, 7 to 7. 
 
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf: The Safe, Healthy, Connected People Commission met on July 14th, a day after 
our last council meeting. We welcomed new commissioners and thanked our outgoing commissioners. 
We reviewed updates to the Comprehensive Plan as it relates to the Safe, Healthy, Connected People 
chapter. That took up the bulk of the meeting and then a really exciting update from Ray that our 
THRIVE afterschool program has been awarded five stars. That’s a huge accomplishment and really 
major kudos to everyone involved in attaining that; thanks so much.  
 
Housing Commission met on the 28th. We also welcomed one new commissioner, and we hopefully will 
appoint another one tonight. We reviewed housing quality and code enforcement work with Chief 
Audy. Had a chance to review some of the data, some of the major concerns and trends that come up. 
Had a chance to look at the ESO data warehouse that used now and answer questions relating to 
housing quality review and frequency of inspections. Another component of the meeting was reviewing 
recent updates to the zoning ordinance (Unified Land Use and Development Regulations – ULUDR) and 
had a discussion/approval for additional lenders for the housing trust fund. The group voted to have 
our Housing Initiative Director explore additional partnerships with North Country Federal Credit Union, 
the Vermont Federal Credit Union, and Community Bank. More to come on that.  
 
The Chittenden Solid Waste District met on July 29th. There was an extensive executive session, after 
which we came out and voted to approve lease equipment for optical sorting, which will help with 
improving the quality of the products that are sorted and go out for market for sale.  
 
Additional meetings will be warned soon. I know that our Safe, Healthy, Connected People meeting will 
be moved because that is typically scheduled for next Tuesday, which would be the night of the 
Primary so we will be adjusting that. Further updates will be through our standard city channel 
notifications.

Councilor Al Turkos:  
 
Airport Commission Meeting 
The next Burlington International Airport Commission meeting is this Wednesday, August 5, at 4:00 
PM.  Meetings are open to the public, and I encourage anyone interested in airport operations, sound 
mitigation, or airport-related issues to attend. You can attend both virtually or in-person.  
 
Inclusion & Belonging Committee 
The next Winooski Inclusion & Belonging Committee will meet on Thursday, August 13, at 6:00 PM. If 
you're interested in helping make Winooski a more welcoming, equitable, and inclusive community, 
we'd love to have you join us. We are also actively looking for new members to join us so please reach 
out to me if you have any questions, or you can apply directly online. 
 
Winooski Clean-Up Day – Saturday, August 8 
Join me for a Winooski Clean-Up Day on Saturday, August 8, from 8:30 – 11:00 AM. We'll meet 
outside Scout Coffee at the top of the circle before heading out to help keep our city beautiful. 
Everyone is welcome—bring a friend, and we'll provide supplies! 
 
A heartfelt thank you to Sarah and everyone who works so hard to set up, break down, and keep our 
Downtown Winooski Block Parties and Farmers Market running so smoothly. These events don't just 
happen, they take an incredible amount of planning and behind-the-scenes work. Thank you to all of 
the staff, volunteers, vendors, musicians, and community members who help make downtown such a 
vibrant place to gather each week.  
 
Councilor Elsie Goodrich: The Winooski Finance Commission met July 14th to discuss the payment 
agreement procedure which governs the rules and responsibility for setting up payment plan for money 
owed to the City such as parking tickets, property taxes, utility bills and other approved charges. 
Payment plans are intended to help people who cannot pay the full amount right away without 
experiencing financial hardship while also protecting the City’s financial interests. The next meeting of 
the Finance Commission, which was to be held on the Primary election date of August 11th will either be 
rescheduled or canceled depending on the availability of the commissioners. 
 
Councilor Eli Ogilvie: Th is month’s Municipal Infrastructure meeting was unfortunately canceled due to 
lack of quorum. With that being said, we were able to get a good turnout for the municipal 
infrastructure open house that occurred on Wednesday, July 29th. I want to thank city staff, the 
Winooski Alliance for Active Transportation, residents and commissioners for showing up and giving 
their input for the comprehensive plan. Your feedback will be the guiding documents our city will use 
over the next decade. Additionally, on July 16th, the Deputy Mayor and I had wonderful conversations 
with residents at our temporary library location. A few items that were brought up were related to 
housing and infrastructure. The main concerns and questions were regarding the need for housing. The 
main questions and interest were related to the addition of more affordable housing and the focus of 
more family housing. There was a focus for more single-family homes as well as town houses and 
green space was considered extremely important for the folks we had.  
 
Regarding infrastructure, there was general excitement for the end of the Main Street construction and 
praise for how it’s coming together. There were questions and concerns regarding the upcoming bridge 
project, and it seems that folks are somewhat unaware of the upcoming street intersection and 
sidewalk extension project on East Spring Street. I want to thank all the folks that we chatted with and 
if you have any more questions, please reach out.

VI. City Updates 
 
Elaine Wang, City Manager, gave the following updates 
 
The City of Winooski is updating our Master Plan. Now known as the “Comprehensive Plan”, this 
document serves as the guide for local government projects and budgeting for the community. If you’re 
new to this concept, cities adopt a comprehensive plan every 8 years. Winooski is due to adopt our 
next one in March of 2027 and need community voices informing the plan! To do this, we’re hosting 
Open House events throughout the summer. The final open house event will take place on Thursday, 
August 27 from 5 – 7 PM at the Winooski Senior Center. This event will focus on the “Safe, Healthy, and 
Connected” area of the Strategic Vision – give feedback on how the City can improve its livability in 
terms of parks, community programming, public health, and public safety. Light refreshments will be 
provided. If you haven’t been able to attend these events, online feedback forms are available at 
winooskivt.gov/plan. 
Speaking of events: 
• We’re hosting our quarterly blood drive at City Hall on Friday, August 14, from 12 - 4:30 PM. Blood 
donations are in critical need – please visit redcrossblood.org or call 1 800 RED CROSS to schedule. 
Participants who donate during this event will receive a $20 Amazon Gift Card – visit winooskivt.gov/news 
to learn more.  
• The 2026 Statewide Primary Election is on Tuesday, August 11, 2026 from 7 AM to 7 PM at the Winooski 
Senior Center. To view the official warning, sample ballots, and to register to vote, visit 
winooskivt.gov/vote. 
• Don’t miss the Friendship Festival on Sunday, August 30, from 2 – 9 PM at the Winooski School District! 
This free family-friendly event is designed to celebrate the people, cultures, and stories that make 
Winooski such a vibrant and welcoming community. Residents and visitors of all ages are invited to spend 
the day connecting with neighbors, enjoying local food, experiencing live performances, and participating 
in activities that bring people together. For full event details, visit 
downtownwinooski.org/friendshipfestival. And, FYI: This event is part of a larger community-strengthening 
initiative supported through the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's Welcoming Communities program and 
the Vermont Community Foundation's Social Cohesion Grant, in partnership with Downtown Winooski and 
the Winooski School District. 
Lastly, a gentle reminder that property tax and utility payments are due August 15. Payments will be 
accepted on time before 8:00 am on Wednesday, August 19th, since City Hall is closed on Monday, August 17, 
for Bennington Battle Day. Postmarks are not accepted as on-time payments. Make your payments online at 
winooskivt.gov/pay or in person at Winooski City Hall. Payment plans, direct debit, and paperless billing are 
available.

Motion: A motion to approve James Paradissis and Jarron Khan, with Jarron being a full-time

Goodrich. Motion passed 4-0. 
 
B. Discussion/Approval: 111 Winooski Falls Way Sign Master Plan Application and Act 250 Permit 
Amendment Application - Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning  
 
Minutes: Doug Nedde gave an introduction and mentioned the hotel is planning to open on September 
21. They shared their appreciation of the processes in place for the signage and shared with Council 
and the public the sign plans.  
 
The Director of City Planning spoke extensively about the applicant proposal and reviewed criteria 
needed with downtown sign code. The sign does not completely conform with the City’s sign code, 
however, there is some flexibility that can be given based on comparisons to apartments and other 
buildings in the vicinity who also have signage. They asked the Council for some latitude due to 
multiple uses of this property. 
 
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf inquired about sign lighting and Doug Nedde mentioned that these signs will not 
have any lighting features included. 
 
Motion: Motion to approve the 111 Winooski Falls Way Sign Master Plan as presented and approve the 
application to submit the Act 250 Permit Application made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and seconded by 
Councilor Turkos. Motion passed 4-0. 
 
C.  Discussion/Approval: Downtown Winooski Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) - Elaine Wang, 
City Manager  
 
Minutes: City Manager Wang gave an overview about the downtown organization and necessity of 
working with them. Melissa Corbin, the Executive Director for Downtown Winooski then gave an 
extensive overview and presentation about Downtown Winooski’s work over the previous year as well 
as the need for their work related to economic vitality, equity, and access, in addition to the 
Downtown Winooski’s program schedule. They also shared some information about sponsorships 
decreasing this current year, yet they are working on finding new funding opportunities. They have 
been working with Vermont’s Department of Liquor and Lottery and have collaborated with Four 
Quarters Brewing on a new revenue opportunity that may be implemented soon. There are currently 
three changes in the MOU that were reviewed and allowed Council to solicit feedback and questions. 
 
The Council shared their appreciation for the work and collaboration efforts the organization has made 
for the city. Deputy Mayor Oakleaf made some suggestions for possible opportunities for sponsorships 
and program ideas. There was further discussion amongst Council members and Downtown Winooski 
related to revising this proposed MOU regarding event coordination with Councilor Turkos and 
Councilor Goodrich both sharing their opinions on the need for having certain events clearly outlined in 
the MOU. There are aspirations to have a minimum number of events in place rather than ambiguity 
for potential celebrations. Downtown Winooski took the suggestions of Council into consideration and 
stated they would appreciate some flexibility in planning future events but understand the need for 
concrete dates for bigger events being established well in advance.

D. Discussion/Approval: Position Descriptions for Assistant Fire Marshal and Career Lieutenant - John 
Audy, Fire Chief and Jesse Acri, Human Resources Director  
 
Minutes: Fire Chief Audy reviewed the position descriptions with Council, as these will better reflect 
operational needs for the Fire Department. The Lieutenant position will be a full twenty four hour (24) 
position and help with a shift in needs for the department’s future operational growth. The benefits of 
having an Assistant Fire Marshal will clarify responsibilities, recruitment, and succession planning for 
the department as well. The Human Resources Director added that there is some appealability for 
these new positions, as there has been a drop in candidates due to the current position descriptions.  
 
The Mayor shared their appreciation to hear that there is interest in fulfilling these new possible 
positions and asked some questions about scheduling. Deputy Mayor Oakleaf also asked about the 
possible impact these new positions would may have on inspections. The Fire Chief was able to 
respond to their questions and clarified that they are confident that these changes can continue to 
support all inspections in the future. 
 
Motion: Motion to approve the Assistant Fire Marshal and Career Lieutenant position descriptions as 
presented made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion passed unanimously 
4-0. 
 
E. Discussion/Approval: Position Description for Thrive Program Assistant Director (Part Time) - Ray 
Coffey, Community Services Director and Jesse Acri, Human Resources Director  
 
Minutes: The Community Services Director mentioned that this item was initially slated for discussion 
during the budget season, but due to the current Thrive Program Director stepping down from the 
position soon, it was important to present this to the Council at this time. The Thrive program recently 
received a five-star designation, and this designation allows for growth with the program. Ray spoke 
about the costs associated with this position as well as the opportunity to allow for growth amongst its 
staff for leadership opportunities. 
 
The Mayor shared their appreciation of the program and asked some questions about offsetting costs 
and current staffing. Deputy Mayor Oakleaf asked questions about the adjusting of positions having 
any possible effects for increasing participation in the program as well as current capacity and the 
need for a waitlist. The Community Services Director was able to answer Council’s questions and 
currently there is not a waitlist; current staffing levels are well above the required ratios, but they are 
expecting continued growth with Thrive. 
 
Motion: Motion to approve the Thrive Program Assistant Director position description as presented 
made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf. Motion carried 4-0.

Initiative Director, Ray Coffey, Community Services Director, Justin Huizenga, Police Chief, John 
Audy, Fire Chief, and Jon Rauscher, Public Works Director

Minutes: Various departments presented to the Council with updates from the fourth quarter of the 
previous fiscal year.  
 
The Community Services Director commented that overall, everything is moving along well. Sidra 
Hoffman, the Trails and Park Steward, has been fabulous with basic maintenance and has been a 
great addition to the team. There is a ton going on behind the scenes which has also made great 
progress. Next week, they are anticipating the Landry Park pavilion walls to be raised. Deputy Mayor 
Oakleaf acknowledged the work the department is doing and asked about the O’Brien Community 
Center, which is currently moving along slower than anticipated, due to fundraising. They have been 
meeting with vendors and planning, which is making progress. Councilor Turkos also gave appreciation 
for the work Sidra has done and commented that it has been wonderful being out in the community 
and appreciates the additional support. 
 
The Fire Chief reviewed recruitment and retention and are excited for some upcoming interviews this 
week. There will be an RFP for EMS services soon and acknowledged St. Michael’s with their 
assistance. On July 1st dispatchers in the Police Department took over fire calls and they acknowledged 
their collaboration and efforts and shared kudos. 
 
The Director of City Planning spoke about impact fees as a tool to offset costs due to added impact 
from development (e.g., a greenfield and five hundred new units could have an impact fee that could 
be leveled for improved levels of service). They have collaborated with Chittenden County Regional 
Planning Commission, which can offer support for impact studies, on how other municipalities work 
with these fees and they are usually tied to new development or expectations of population growth. 
Impact fees are tied to impact growth, and the benefits could be used for the whole city or just a 
portion but must be proportional. The Mayor gave thanks for the work done on this item and noted 
that residents have some concerns about growth and seeing some repercussions of previous impact 
fees. Deputy Mayor Oakleaf then had a discussion related to growth, line striping, and road use and 
how to mitigate the adverse impacts. Councilor Ogilvie asked about the scope of the impact fee and 
the Director of City Planning clarified that it depends on specific capital items and what exactly the 
benefit is for. Further discussion ensued related to specific examples, projections, and calculations with 
the Public Works Director sharing input related to water and sewer projects.  
 
The Housing Initiative Director talked about policies that are proceeding as planned. Some highlights 
include effective collaboration efforts with the Housing and Planning Commissions. In addition, the 
housing needs assessment is currently in the community engagement phase. They mentioned some 
updates related to the Armory project with more information coming. Short-term rentals ended with 
only one property out of compliance (fiscal, not code), as well as the City’s first property complaint 
related to an electrical issue, which is a great first step in this process. The total number of licenses at 
the end of the fiscal year totaled fifty-four. Lastly, more information related to airport noise mitigation 
will be presented on September 21. 
 
The Finance Director spoke about the cross-cutting update, and specifically about focus groups. There 
is a new onboarding process to compensate focus groups without filling out paperwork.  
 
City Manager Wang shared their appreciation for the equity component from the work Jazmine and 
Angela did. In addition, they shared information related to parking, as they are not having any luck 
with the volume of parking space agreements. They will be following up with larger landlords soon to 
gauge interest.
